newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel gains on dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel gains on dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose on Monday against the dollar and the basket of foreign currencies in nervous and volatile trading, dealers said.
"Trading was very volatile today and the market is showing nervousness. The dollar rose from 3.2580 shekels to 3.2660 only to fall later to 3.2500 shekels," said Gideon Sadeh at Bank Leumi.
"There is no clear trend in the market and every big deal moves the market as investors try to guess where the market is going," Sadeh said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2490 shekels against 3.2670 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.6477 shekels against 3.6644 on Friday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8708 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8737 on Friday and against the mark at 2.1468 shekels against 2.1508 on Friday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2530 shekels.
